services.name: Standard peptide COA (purity, identity and mass)
Blend analysis (for example BPC-157 + GHK-Cu + TB-500)

caveats: The site describes itself as Canada's only dedicated domestic peptide testing lab. Several other Canadian labs in this directory also test peptides domestically, so treat that as marketing rather than fact.
No laboratory street address, and no named accreditation body: the site says "licensed" and "validated following USP principles", which is not the same as an accredited scope.
"20 years experience" and "100% accurate testing" are the site's own claims and are not independently audited.

pricingSummary: CA$249 a peptide, CA$275 a blend, with every add-on priced in the catalogue. New orders are paused as of 2026-11-14; see the notice above.

VialTests describes itself as a testing service brand operating a laboratory, not as an accredited laboratory in its own right.

name: Testides
pricingSummary: CA$280 a sample for the standard panel, CA$250 each at three or more, with endotoxin and metals at CA$100 each.

services.name: Standard panel
services.price: CA$280 per sample, CA$250 each at 3 or more

turnaround: Not published on the public portal
caveats: The public marketing site is gone. There is no services page, no price page and no laboratory address to read: everything now lives behind the portal, and this entry was reconstructed from the portal's own JavaScript bundle.
Testides chooses a laboratory for you to submit to. It is a routing and reporting layer, not a single named facility, and this directory previously described it as a laboratory.
The portal warns that an Interac e-Transfer must not mention peptides in the notice, and that a transfer from a company whose name contains "peptides" will be rejected. Plan the payment accordingly.
No published turnaround, and no named accreditation.
A blend can be submitted, but the portal never says the components are resolved and quantified separately. If you need a per-component result rather than one averaged figure, ask before shipping.

name: Maple Leaf Diagnostics
pricingSummary: CA$250 for identity, quantity and purity. Endotoxin is CA$100.
notices: Read 2026-09-11: Maple Leaf posted a notice dated 8 September 2026 pausing all new testing because of a backlog, with testing to resume in October, and said it is relocating its offices and will not be following up on email until the move and the backlog are cleared. Confirm it is accepting samples before you ship one, and confirm the address before you address the parcel.
caveats: Testing is paused as of 8 September 2026 and the laboratory is mid-move. See the notice above.
Purity is by HPLC-UV/DAD with MS for identity, not by tandem MS quantitation against a calibration curve. That is a different and cheaper measurement from the one SideChain and VialTests describe.
This directory previously recorded "no published price list". The prices above are on the services page and were missed.

The catalogue prices are for reference standards you buy, not for testing you order.

Sterility is not offered, and no accreditation is stated on the site.

The compendial microbiology here is the same USP chapter number as the cheaper add-ons elsewhere in this directory. The difference is the quality system around it, and the price reflects that.

The archive count is stated differently on different pages of the same site, from over 40,000 to over 42,000 to a live counter above 69,000 on 2026-11-14, so read it as tens of thousands rather than as one figure.
The site states no vendor affiliations. That is its own claim and is not independently audited.

Peptides are one service line among many. This is a compliance laboratory that tests peptides, not a peptide laboratory.

caveats: Testing is available to US residents only, and shipments from outside the US are refused. This entry is here for the published ratings, which anyone can read, not because a Canadian reader can send a vial.

Finnrick is a programme and a publisher, not a laboratory. The partner laboratories are named, and Finnrick describes two of them (Harrens Lab and PharmLabs) as ISO/IEC 17025 accredited; that is Finnrick's description, so check the accrediting body and scope with the laboratory itself before relying on it.
The verification page requires a free account, and original laboratory PDFs for published tests are a paid membership feature.
The ratings are Finnrick's own analysis and, in its own words, are not an endorsement. A ratings position is a claim by a third party, not a measurement of the vial you hold.
Finnrick's help pages state that sales are final, with no refunds after payment.
